- Model tends to overestimate prices in the short term (especially after recent spikes) and underestimates during sustained downward sentiment.
- When sentiment is negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model should reduce forecasted peak values and shift toward mean-reversion paths.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots the true value — apply a 10–15% downward correction for the next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are falling, model should not assume continuation — expect mean reversion toward prior 10-day average.
- Model underreacts to strong negative sentiment — when sentiment < -0.6 for 3+ days, reduce forecast by 5–10% and add a downward bias of 0.5–1.0 standard deviation.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture the “tail risk” of sudden drops — add a 1–2% buffer for downward volatility if sentiment is volatile or negative.
- If true outcome is below 30% of 30-day moving average, model should not assume continuation — expect a correction in next 5–7 periods.
- Model overconfident in upward trends — if sentiment is mixed or neutral, reduce forecast slope by 20–30% to avoid overestimating momentum.
